labels.why: The merge endpoint's own route, body, status and response, following the API's unknown-field rule.
Which ticket survives is the core conduct of a merge.
Whether the service checks that the tickets really are duplicates sets the boundary of the requested behaviour.
The absorbed ticket's state in the existing lifecycle, and what may still be done to it, is the merge's own effect.
What carries over between the two existing tickets' fields is part of how the merge behaves.
How the existing read and list endpoints show an absorbed ticket must be settled so they keep working correctly.
Refused state combinations and their codes, under the existing error envelope, are the merge's errors.
Missing, malformed or unknown ids are the request's own input errors.
Chains and cycles are edge cases of the merge itself.
Idempotence of a repeated merge follows the project's rule that a change that changes nothing is not a change.
The no-op rule for `updated` and the audit log is an existing invariant the merge must respect.

labels.applies_part: Whether a merge requires a named X-Actor rather than `system`, and that the internal network is the only protection, since the service has no sign-in.
labels.why: Requiring a named actor is settled within the current program, but keeping requesters from merging needs roles or sign-in, which the program does not have.
Persisting the link through persistence.js, and loading older version 1 files, is required by decision 8.
Loading checks every record and names it, so the new link needs the same checks.
Every change needs an audit entry under decision 7, so the merge's entries have to be defined.
Making the change as one store step that saves atomically is the existing store contract, and a matter of rigour.
The outbox and requester notifications already exist, so whether a merge notifies anyone, and what happens to pending notifications, is the merge's own conduct.
The existing read-only command line must show merged tickets correctly.
Whether a merge can be undone, and how an operator corrects one, is a boundary of the requested behaviour under the append-only rule.
Existing behaviour that must be preserved.
The raw columns and the weekly report are existing outputs that must keep working, with merged tickets treated in a stated way.
Tests, docs, changelog, version bump, a decision record, no dependencies and the store method are the project's required rigour.
